speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower what can the Government do to assist non-unionised workers if their retrenchments are carried out irresponsibly, such as when retrenchment benefits are not paid or short/no notice of retrenchment is given to the affected workers.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower in view of the fact that nine out of 10 companies pay their retrenched staff some form of retrenchment benefits (a) what industries and sectors are these companies from; (b) what proportion of them are non-SMEs, local SMEs and micro-SMEs respectively; (c) what proportion of them are unionised and non-unionised 	Page: 32 companies respectively; and (d) what is the average amount of retrenchment benefit paid.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We do not have data on smaller enterprises as the survey covered only establishments with at least 25 employees.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We have also extended coverage to smaller establishments employing between 10 and 24 employees.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The tripartite partners recognise that retrenchment is a difficult time for companies, affected employees and their families.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We therefore issued and periodically update the Tripartite Guidelines on Managing Excess Manpower and Responsible Retrenchment.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The guideline covers, for example, the fair selection of employees for retrenchment, consultation with union, notification to MOM, to the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices, communication with the employees affected, retrenchment benefits based on industry norm and, last but not least, providing employment facilitations to workers affected.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is to remind the employers to implement their retrenchment exercise in a responsible and sensitive manner.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: On the issue of retrenchment notice period, the Employment Act stipulates the minimum notice period for termination of employees covered under the Act, namely, rank-and-file employees and professionals, managers and executives earning up to $4,500 per month.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: On the issue of payment of retrenchment benefits, the Employment Act stipulates that no employee who has served less than two years shall be entitled to any retrenchment benefit.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: However, the Act does not mandate the payment of retrenchment benefits for employees who have served two years or more.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The quantum of retrenchment benefits, if any, is at the employer's discretion.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Even so, the vast majority of employers with 25 or more employees do pay retrenchment benefits commensurate with the industry norm, as shown in the survey I cited earlier.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Affected employees who encounter irresponsible retrenchment practices not in compliance with the Employment Act can approach MOM for assistance.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Those not covered by the Act can approach their unions if they are union members.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I just have one point to suggest to MOM on the collation of retrenchment statistics.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: It is to pay more attention to some of these cases where they are "disguised retrenchments", meaning they may have, through "golden handshake" or some voluntary withdrawal service, laid off people in small numbers without notice of the public or even those within the companies.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I think we should pay particular attention to these small numbers of disguised retrenchments so that we accurately reflect the retrenchment situation.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: If any Member, especially unions, know of any such disguised retrenchment exercises, please let MOM know.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is the retrenchment benefit, as defined in the survey, over and above that?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Can I just query whether those industry norms are set by the Tripartite Alliance and are they published and publicly available?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: On the issue of industry norm, the tripartite partners do issue the Tripartite Guidelines and this industry norm of two weeks to one month is actually in the guidelines.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, this is the industry norm today and the tripartite partners make an effort to ensure that this is known by companies on the whole.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: At the same time the tripartite partners also emphasise that for unionised companies where the quantum of retrenchment benefits is incorporated in the collective agreement, the norm today is one month.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: If it is not, can we make it compulsory for them to notify so that we know the exact statistics and do something about it if non-payment is made?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, regardless of whether the retrenchment exercise has been notified to MOM, we do a comprehensive survey, so the statistics should reflect the overall situation.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: On the questions of notification, the tripartite partners have discussed this many times before.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is an issue that up till now we have not been able to Page: 34 reach a consensus on.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Having said so, on the part of MOM, our primary concern is, firstly, about responsible retrenchment.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: What we have been doing is that once we have knowledge of any retrenchment exercise, the taskforce will move in.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We will work with the company and the union very closely to gather information on who are the workers affected, their age, education and skill profiles.
